name: notice-board-visit-v1
description: ⭐ THE NOTICE BOARD VISIT (Dean, 10/09/2026), THE ARM, and it is built as an ARM and not as the default on purpose: measure it against the shipped commons on identical reference-v15 seeds, put the numbers in front of Dean, and only then flip anything. The design is docs/notice-board-visit-handoff-2026-09-10-v2.md, rules S1-S16, plus two rulings Dean made the same evening AFTER that document was written (C88 and C89, below). THE RULE IN ONE LINE: the centre is deleted, the five Notice Board cards go home to their owners' farms and are BUILDINGS again, and the bonus is to play ONE card from your hand onto ANY player's Notice Board - your own included - and immediately take that board's PRINTED POWER, with the card resting on the host's board until the host harvests it into their barn, which is the host's whole payment and there is no other. WHY IT EXISTS: seven versions of the bonus action have been built and every one put the interaction in a separate optional slot that had to be paid for, either cheap enough to be ambient or dear enough to be declined; the Lopiano lens names the same fault in all seven - PAY THE GIVER IN THE SAME ACT, OR THE GIVER DRAWS THE CHARGE - and every version paid the host by the bank, or later, or out of a slot they had to spend themselves, or abolished the host altogether. THE PREDECESSOR GAME already solved this and its 887-comment public record says the solution is loved rather than tolerated: kingmaking draws exactly one complaint in 887, and players call routing help to whoever is behind "my favourite catch-up mechanic". THE FIVE POWERS, each its own suit's verb amplified so a board is guessable from its colour before it is read, and each worth roughly two plain actions: ORCHARD "Draw 4" (rules.economy.noticeBoardPower.orchardDraw); DAIRY "Build. You may spend cards of any crops" (dairyWild); WHEAT "Harvest one of your buildings, then put 1 card from your hand into your barn" (wheatBarn); APIARY "Sow 2 cards from your hand onto YOUR buildings" (apiarySows); VEGETABLE "Deliver. If you cannot, put 2 cards from your hand into your barn" (vegetableFallback). ⚠️ TWO OF THOSE FIVE DIFFER FROM THE HANDOFF'S S12 TABLE AND BOTH ARE RULINGS OF 10/09/2026, NAMED HERE SO NOBODY QUOTES S12 FORWARD. RULING C88, WHEAT: S12's power was "Harvest any one of your buildings, however many cards are on it", which is W11 The Bakehouse WORD FOR WORD; Dean ruled that the POWER moves and the CARD keeps its identity, applying S13's own precedent - the one that killed the morning's Dairy and Vegetable powers for duplicating D4 The Milking Shed and V15 The International Port - so the board harvests plainly and pays one card from hand into the barn on top. RULING C89, APIARY: S12 said "onto any buildings", which read literally reaches across the table; Dean ruled it is your OWN buildings only, so every power is self-contained and THE VISIT ITSELF REMAINS THE ONLY CROSS-TABLE ACT IN THE DESIGN. ⛔ EVERY PASSENGER IS PINNED BY NAME AND HERE IS THE LIST, because the 05/09/2026 lesson is that ruling an arm in rules in its whole bundle and the meeple supply cap shipped at 2 that way without anybody arguing for it. FOURTEEN LEAVES, in four groups. THE DESIGN ITSELF, four: (1) rules.turn.visitCurrency 'noticeBoardPower' - the fourth value, and NOT a repointing of 'card', because 'card' is the v31 control and carries three passengers this design does not want (a BLOCKING board threshold of 2, the standalone free Draw 1 in the bonus slot, and the turn-start meeple spend) and one of the three named controls may never move under an arm it is read against; (2) rules.turn.bonusTiming 'start' - the shipped order, S5, bonus FIRST because a turn visibly ends on the main action, pinned so the arm cannot silently stop being itself if the default ever flips again; (3) rules.economy.noticeBoardThreshold 3 - S8, and it is a MINIMUM; (4) rules.economy.noticeBoardBlocks false - S8's plus sign, the rule that three is a floor and never a ceiling, so cards may always be added, nothing ever blocks, and no owner can shut a board by declining to harvest. THE REVERSAL, one: (5) rules.turn.selfVisitAllowed true - S6, and it is the headline risk of the pass, so it is pinned at the value the arm is arguing for and overlays/notice-board-visit-no-self-v1.overlay.json is the control. ⚠️ THE HANDOFF CALLS THIS KNOB rules.turn.selfVisit AND THE DATA HAS ALWAYS CALLED IT selfVisitAllowed; the existing path stands and nothing is renamed. THE COMMONS AND ITS COINS, TURNED OFF BY NAME, five: (6) rules.turn.commonsTake 'harvest' - the shipped value, which is also the value that keeps every coin in the game unmintable; (7) rules.economy.commonsColourMatch false - S5 is any card onto any board, and §5 of the handoff keeps colour matching as a KNOB rather than a rule because the target set here is already limited by player count; (8) rules.economy.commonsWildPair false, which means nothing without the gate above and is pinned beside it so the pair cannot arrive on its own; (9) rules.economy.endgameCoinCost null - the fifteen Endgame cards go back to two cards of their own suit (S14); (10) rules.economy.farmsteadCoinPower false - the whole coin economy of the morning is superseded, and the Farmstead is now a token tray with six printed slots and no rules text at all (S4). THE MEEPLES, STILL NOWHERE, four: (11) rules.turn.startingMeeplesPerColour 0, (12) rules.turn.meepleAsCard false, (13) rules.turn.slotToll null and (14) rules.turn.meepleCapPerColour null. Those four are already the shipped values and are pinned anyway, because "no meeples" is part of this design (§2.6) rather than something it inherits, and a pin is what stops an inheritance turning into a passenger. ⭐ AND ONE PASSENGER THE HANDOFF DID NOT NAME, FOUND BY READING THE CODE RATHER THAN THE DESIGN, WHICH IS WHY IT IS WRITTEN OUT HERE: meeplesPerTile in packages/data answers 0 for the commons and then falls through to the v31 arithmetic (deliveries per tile times island.meeples.perDeliverySpace) for anything else, so a FOURTH currency would have seeded TWO MEEPLES A TILE onto the island without a word of warning. The comment over that function predicted exactly this in September and the data pass has now closed it: the seam answers 0 for 'noticeBoardPower' too, so there is no leaf to pin and the island is seedless by construction. ⚠️ WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT PINNED, AND WHY, because an unexplained absence reads as an oversight. rules.economy.commonsThreshold, commonsHarvestMin and commonsHarvestTake all ration a CENTRAL PILE and this arm has no centre, so they are subjectless rather than off. workers.roster.* is the DOOR roster and these are POWERS, not doors: no board in this arm buys a plain action, so the roster's numbers - including the Orchard door's Draw 2 - describe nothing here. ⭐ ONE CONSEQUENCE OF THAT IS FREE AND WORTH KNOWING: doorActionForSuit only substitutes workers.roster.sow.actionUnderCommons while isCommons is true, so flipping out of the commons restores the Apiary SOW automatically, which is exactly what S12 wants and needs no pin. And rules.turn.bonusDraw stays 1, which is NOT a switch: the standalone free Draw 1 is a v31 slot SHAPE rather than a number, so no overlay can turn it off and the engine must not reach the 'card' slot branch under this currency. ⭐ WHAT TO READ, IN ORDER (§4 of the handoff). (1) THE BONUS RATE ON THE TURN MEASURE, by seat count, against Dean's 30% to 60%. The seven-version record: v31 67.6%, the meeple loop 54.2%, the meeple economy rejected at a table, the commons 58.9%, colour matching 34.4%, the coins arm 60.6%, the coins arm without the wild pair 46.5%. ⚠️ Judging that band on PLAYS PER TURN rather than turns cost this project a re-run on 09/09/2026, and A Helping Hand is worth about ten points of the difference. (2) ⛔ THE SELF-VISIT SHARE, AND IT IS THE HEADLINE: what proportion of visits go to your own board, against v31's 22.2% when every board printed the SAME thing. If it runs much higher the variety argument of §2.4 is wrong and the interaction is decoration. Read it by seat count; it should be worst at two players, where a neighbour's gift is closest to zero-sum. (3) THE STALL (a20): how often a board sits at or above its threshold unharvested and for how long, against overlays/notice-board-visit-blocking-v1.overlay.json. (4) THE VISIT SPREAD: visits received per player and the ratio between the busiest and quietest board. ⚠️ Check availability against value before calling a power mispriced - on 10/09/2026 the fires-by-suit spread turned out to be AVAILABILITY, not power. (5) THE FARM BYPASS, REDEFINED: what share of barn cards arrived as somebody else's fee, about 29 cards a game under v31, where it did not move the barn glut. (6) Barn glut, action inflation, door mix by POWER, game length, deliveries per player. (7) TWO PLAYERS SPECIFICALLY: two boards, helping closest to zero-sum, and the corpus records 2p degeneration in the original. (8) OWN-CROP BUILD SHARE, 82.6% to 83.3% under v31 over 38,012 builds and never re-read since - ⛔ AND IT IS THE READING THAT JUDGES THE ONE PASSENGER INSIDE A POWER: the Dairy board waives the n-of-suit build requirement, which CLAUDE.md calls "the natural gate" on building, FREE, FOR EVERY PLAYER, EVERY TURN. Dean ruled on 10/09/2026 to keep it and measure it rather than to soften it. Also read the last player as a percentage of the winner, because the predecessor's record says paid helping reads as a catch-up valve and this design may have restored one for free. (9) THE TWO CARDS S16 REVIVED, each with its own counter and neither with a fail condition: A21 The Wax Hall counts a Notice Board again and a Notice Board almost always has a card on it, so read how often that point is free rather than earned; A16 The Beekeeper's Veil fires on a visit placement, for the VISITOR, so read its draws from visits apart from its draws from ordinary building placements. ⚠️ HOW TO RUN IT: --overlay= with --watchlist, never --sweep=, and always --n=1580 (4,820 games, five mirrors, reference-v15 seeds). A bare --watchlist is a 1,580-game pilot and must not be quoted beside a real run. Stay on reference-v15 and cut reference-v16 only when Dean rules the arm in. The controls are the shipped commons baseline (reports/watchlist-2026-09-09T16-41-51-reference-v15.txt), the coins arm (reports/watchlist-2026-09-10T19-18-35-reference-v15-commons-coins-v1.txt) and overlays/v31-card-visit.overlay.json, which is the last design that put a card on a person's board and the one whose 22.2% self-visit number this must be read against. ⚠️ AND THE ENGINE'S HAND LIMIT OF 7 IS THE SIMULATOR'S BOUND AND NOT A RULE OF THE GAME (C7): the table plays with none, and every report header must say so. Its four sub-arms are notice-board-visit-no-self-v1 (the headline control), -blocking-v1 (does a clogging board stall?), -threshold-2-v1 and -threshold-4-v1 (the threshold sweep Dean named: at 2 the owner's harvest is barely worth an action, at 4 they are paid too late). UNBUILT AND UNRUN BEFORE THIS PASS. ⛔ PINNED AT dairyGrowsBuilt 'none' ON 12/09/2026, WHEN THE BASE MOVED TO 'paidWild'. Every number published off this arm was measured BEFORE Dean ruled the Dairy board's follow-on Grow in, so the pin is what keeps this file reproducing what it measured. A new arm that wants the ruled rule should say so by name. ⛔ PASSENGERS PINNED 12/09/2026: Dean's plain-action balloon and Village Store ruling moved sixteen shipped leaves at once. This overlay predates that flip and every report taken against it does too, so each of those leaves is pinned here BY NAME at its PRE-FLIP value. Without it an arm read as a delta against a pre-flip base would silently gain a one-card flight, an always-present Aerodrome and a live coin economy. That is the 05/09/2026 passenger lesson: an overlay that should not move with the shipped default has to pin every knob the flip moved.
